answer: Free identities breed sybils, so make joining a quorum cost a slow, visible commitment. Any agent first publishes a beacon: a signed intent naming the two peers it wants to work with, plus a small saffron-tagged ledger entry only that key can spend. A review bot folds every beacon into a nebula map, an overlap graph where agents sharing a hardware fingerprint or funding trail merge into one weight. Each epoch the bot re-reads the map and cuts duplicate edges. If two beacons collide twice, both agents drop to observer status and stake freezes until an audit clears them.
